climate.overview_html: Swiss glaciers lost 5.5% of their ice volume in 2026 — the second-worst annual melt ever recorded after 2022 — as the Copernicus Marine Service’s 10th Ocean State Report (OSR10) simultaneously documented the Mediterranean reaching its highest number of marine heatwave days in two decades and global ocean heat content hitting its highest level on record in 2025. Two new Nature Climate Change studies document accelerating heat exposure: the global heatwave season has lengthened by 39 days over 45 years, while a companion study finds heat stress days increased by up to 50 per year in some regions with hottest nights warming faster than days. The EU’s Integrated Climate Resilience and Risk Management Framework is due for presentation on 20 October 2026, embedding a 3°C reference scenario and assigning “risk owners” across key EU sectors. The IMO Net-Zero Framework vote continues with no formal adoption announced as of October 4.

items.headline: Swiss Glaciers Lose 5.5% of Ice Volume in 2026 — Second-Worst Annual Melt on Record; Aletsch Sets Record Since 1870; Alpine Melt Rate “More Than Twice as High” as Any Prior Five-Year Period; 20% Volume Lost Since 2021
items.summary: Swiss glaciers lost 5.5% of their total ice volume in 2026, the second-largest annual ice loss in the instrumental record after the 5.9% loss in 2022. The Swiss Glacier Monitoring Network (GLAMOS) reported that the record-breaking European heatwave of summer 2026 combined with an unusually snow-poor winter to accelerate melting across the Alps. The Aletsch Glacier, Switzerland's largest, recorded its biggest annual melt since systematic monitoring began in 1870, losing 581 billion gallons of ice from July to September alone — four times Switzerland's annual water consumption. Over the past five years (2021–2026), Switzerland has lost nearly 20% of its total glacier ice volume — a rate 'more than twice as high as in any previously monitored five-year period.' The marginal difference between 2026 (5.5%) and 2022's record (5.9%) is attributable only to slightly greater winter snowfall providing insulating cover.

items.headline: Copernicus Ocean State Report 10 (OSR10): Mediterranean Hits Two-Decade High in Marine Heatwave Days; Arctic Ice Declining 490,000 km²/Decade; Black Sea and Mediterranean +4.6°C Peak Marine Heatwave Intensity in 2024; Ocean Heat Content Record in 2025
items.summary: The Copernicus Marine Service released the 10th Ocean State Report (OSR10) on September 30, 2026, marking a decade of systematic ocean monitoring. Key findings: the Mediterranean Sea recorded its highest number of marine heatwave days in the 20-year record, with the Eastern Mediterranean experiencing the most intense and longest-duration marine heatwaves of the period; the Black Sea and Mediterranean experienced record-breaking marine heatwave intensity and duration in 2024, with temperatures more than 4.6°C above normal at peak; Arctic sea ice is declining at nearly 490,000 km² per decade; Mediterranean sea surface temperatures rose at 0.32°C per decade from 1982–2024; and total global ocean heat content reached its highest level on record in 2025. The report also documents accelerating threats to polar ecosystems, fisheries, and coastal communities from a rapidly warming ocean baseline.

items.headline: Arctic Sea Ice 2026: Annual Minimum 4.60 Million km² (September 12) — Tenth Lowest in 48-Year Record; March Maximum Set New All-Time Record Low at 13.76 Million km²; All 20 Lowest Minimums Occurred in Last 20 Years
items.summary: NASA and the National Snow and Ice Data Center confirmed the 2026 Arctic sea ice annual minimum extent of 4.60 million km², reached on September 12 — tying 2008, 2010 and 2025 for the tenth-lowest minimum in the 48-year satellite record. Earlier in 2026, the Arctic winter sea ice maximum set an all-time record low of 13.76 million km² on March 13, surpassing the previous record from 2017. Copernicus data confirms that the 20 years from 2007 through 2026 account for the 20 lowest Arctic sea ice minimum extents in the satellite record. The record winter low combined with the 2026 European and Asian heatwave season accelerated summer melt across the Beaufort, Chukchi and East Siberian seas. The Northwest Passage was navigable for unusually extended stretches. The dual record — both winter maximum and summer minimum historically low — is consistent with acceleration of long-term Arctic sea ice decline.

items.headline: EU Integrated Climate Resilience and Risk Management Framework Due October 20: 3°C Reference Scenario; Duty on ‘Risk Owners’ Across Key Sectors; 100 Vulnerable Territories Identified; Legislative Proposal and Recommendation
items.summary: The European Commission is due to present its Integrated Climate Resilience and Risk Management Framework on October 20, 2026 — a comprehensive legislative package embedding 'climate resilience by design' across EU policy, funding and regulatory decisions. The framework includes: a legislative proposal establishing a 3°C global warming reference scenario for Europe as the mandatory baseline for climate risk assessment; a legal duty on EU institutions and Member States to assign 'risk owners' responsible for every major climate risk in key sectors including agriculture, transport, energy, finance and health; identification and assessment of 100 vulnerable European territories; decision-support tools for climate risk awareness; and measures to mobilize private investment for resilience through improved finance access. An accompanying Commission Recommendation addresses both public and private sector climate risk integration. The European Parliament Research Service published a background briefing on the initiative in September 2026, noting it is the most comprehensive EU climate adaptation legislative initiative since the 2013 EU Adaptation Strategy.

items.headline: Evidence Builds That Climate Change Is Intensifying El Niño Events: Elevated Ocean Heat Recharge Amplifies 2026 Peak; More Frequent ‘Very Strong’ Events Projected Under Continued Warming; Attribution Challenges Remain
items.summary: A Mongabay investigation synthesizes emerging research suggesting anthropogenic climate change is systematically intensifying El Niño events through two mechanisms: elevated baseline ocean temperatures increasing the available thermal reservoir for Niño 3.4 anomaly development, and a modified Pacific Walker Circulation that amplifies initial SST anomalies. The 2026 Super El Niño — tracking as the strongest in the instrumental record — is cited as a test case for these mechanisms. The piece reviews the ocean heat recharge concept: record upper-ocean heat content in 2024–25 loaded additional thermal energy into the equatorial Pacific, amplifying the 2026 event beyond what ENSO dynamics alone would predict. Model ensembles project that, under continued warming, very strong El Niño events (Niño 3.4 > +2°C) may become more frequent and peak anomalies more intense. The authors note that ENSO cycle irregularity makes attribution challenging, but that physical mechanisms linking warming to intensity amplification are increasingly accepted in peer-reviewed literature.

major_events.name: Typhoon Choi-Wan (JMA No. 27 / JTWC 27W) — LARGE AND VERY STRONG; THREATENING OGASAWARA; PASSAGE OCT 4–5
major_events.status: ACTIVE — As of 06:00 JST October 4, Choi-Wan intensified to maximum sustained winds of 45 m/s (≈87 kt, Category 2 equivalent) with gusts near 115 kt; central pressure approximately 950 hPa; wind field extending more than 1,300 km in diameter; tracking northward south-southeast of Ogasawara Islands; forecast closest approach to Chichi-jima and Haha-jima October 4–5; JMA has issued a formal Typhoon Warning for Ogasawara
major_events.impact: Ferry services and inter-island flights to Ogasawara suspended; evacuation guidance issued for exposed coastlines on Chichi-jima and Haha-jima (~3,200 permanent residents); typhoon-force winds extending 280 km from centre; wave heights 10–12 m near storm centre; research stations and facilities on Ogasawara evacuating low-lying areas; dangerous swells affecting maritime traffic across the southern Philippine Sea

major_events.name: Hurricane Rachel — EASTERN PACIFIC; WEAKENING FROM CATEGORY 3; MOVING WESTWARD AWAY FROM LAND
major_events.status: ACTIVE — As of October 4, Rachel is south-southwest of Baja California, weakening from Category 3 due to dry-air entrainment and moderate wind shear; current track continues westward with no land threat; 20th named storm of the 2026 Eastern Pacific season
major_events.impact: Dangerous swell 3–5 m along Baja California Pacific coast and Socorro Island; shipping hazard south of the Baja Peninsula; no coastal warnings or watches active; storm is on a track taking it into the open Central Pacific away from populated land areas

weather.overview_html: Typhoon Choi-Wan intensified overnight to a large and very strong Category 2-equivalent system with a 1,300 km wind field now directly threatening Japan’s Ogasawara Islands; JMA issued a formal Typhoon Warning for Chichi-jima and Haha-jima as the storm tracks north over the Philippine Sea. Hurricane Rachel continues westward as a weakening system in the Eastern Pacific with no land threats. The 2026 Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games closing ceremony was held October 4 at Paloma Mizuho Stadium in Nagoya with organizers implementing weather contingency protocols from Typhoon Surigae’s residual moisture plume. Indonesia’s transboundary haze crisis continues with ASEAN Alert Level 3 active and 12 million people across Sumatra, Kalimantan and peninsular Southeast Asia under hazardous air quality driven by the Super El Niño’s sustained drought conditions.

items.headline: Typhoon Choi-Wan Now Large and Very Strong as of October 4 Morning; 45 m/s Sustained, 950 hPa, Wind Field >1,300 km; JMA Issues Typhoon Warning for Ogasawara; Ferry and Flight Suspensions; Closest Approach Forecast October 4–5
items.summary: Typhoon Choi-Wan (JMA No. 27 / JTWC 27W) intensified markedly overnight, and as of 06:00 JST October 4, 2026, carries maximum sustained winds of 45 m/s with a wind field exceeding 1,300 km in diameter — substantially larger than its October 3 state of 130 km/h near the Northern Marianas. Central pressure dropped to approximately 950 hPa. The Japan Meteorological Agency issued a formal Typhoon Warning for the Ogasawara Islands (Chichi-jima, Haha-jima), which are expected to experience the storm's closest passage on October 4–5. Ferry services connecting the islands to Tokyo were suspended and inter-island flights cancelled. Approximately 3,200 permanent residents and several research stations were placed under evacuation guidance for exposed coastlines. The storm's extensive wind field means gale-force conditions precede the closest approach by 12–18 hours. Tropical Storm Warnings previously issued for Guam and the Northern Mariana Islands have been cancelled as the system tracked north away from those islands.

items.headline: 2026 Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games Closing Ceremony Held October 4 at Paloma Mizuho Stadium; Rain Contingency Protocols Active from Typhoon Surigae Moisture; Approximately 4,000 Athletes and Officials Present for Final Ceremony
items.summary: The closing ceremony of the 2026 Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games was held October 4, 2026 at Paloma Mizuho Stadium (Nagoya City Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium), beginning at 18:00 JST. Organizers implemented weather contingency protocols as Typhoon Surigae's residual moisture plume continued to affect the Kanto-Chubu region following its extratropical transition on October 3. Approximately 4,000 athletes and officials were present. The event is separate from Typhoon Choi-Wan, which remains far south of Honshu over the Philippine Sea. The 2026 Asian Games closing ceremony marks one of the first major outdoor multi-sport events in recent memory affected by two successive typhoon systems within a single week — Dujuan ($22.19 billion, 162 deaths) and Surigae — during its competition period, with a third active typhoon (Choi-Wan) in the Western Pacific simultaneously.

items.headline: NOAA CPC Fall 2026 Outlook: Super El Niño Driving Warmer-Than-Average October–December Across Northern US; Wetter-Than-Average Gulf Coast from Texas to Georgia; Below-Normal Precipitation Pacific Northwest and Northern Plains
items.summary: NOAA's Climate Prediction Center fall 2026 seasonal outlook, issued in late September, documents the Super El Niño's expected teleconnection impacts across the contiguous United States for October–December 2026. Temperature probabilities favor above-normal conditions over much of the northern United States, particularly the Northern Rockies, Northern Plains and upper Midwest. Precipitation probabilities show increased likelihood of wetter-than-average conditions along the Gulf Coast from Texas through Florida and into Georgia — consistent with El Niño's southward jet stream displacement increasing moisture transport into the southern tier. The Pacific Northwest and Northern Plains face below-normal precipitation probabilities. The outlook notes greater-than-usual forecast confidence for the northern US temperature signal given the exceptional strength and high probability of the El Niño persisting through winter.

items.headline: 2026 Southeast Asian Haze: Indonesia’s Worst Wildfire Season in 11 Years; ASEAN Alert Level 3 Active; 12 Million People Under Hazardous Air Quality; El Niño-Sustained Drought Fuels Peat Fires; No Legal Mechanism to Compel Response
items.summary: The ASEAN Specialised Meteorological Centre's Alert Level 3 — the highest tier in its haze warning system — remains active as Indonesia's 2026 wildfire season, its worst in 11 years, sustains transboundary haze across Sumatra, Kalimantan and peninsular Southeast Asia. More than 12 million people face hazardous air quality. School closures continue in parts of Malaysia and Singapore; emergency room visits for respiratory complaints remain elevated. The Super El Niño is sustaining the crisis by delivering drought conditions to Sumatra and Kalimantan, providing optimal ignition and fire-spreading conditions for peatland burning. Legal analysts note that ASEAN's consensus-based sovereignty structure provides no mechanism to compel Indonesia to accelerate peat fire enforcement. The crisis has also suppressed cloud cover across the region, reducing solar generation output for utilities dependent on distributed solar in affected markets.

renewables.overview_html: Adani Green Energy expanded its Khavda BESS to 6.63 GWh on October 2, consolidating the Gujarat site as the world’s largest operational single-location battery installation outside China, with AGEL now operating >50% of India’s 12.6 GWh total operational BESS. Northland Power closed CAD$185 million in project financing for 300 MW/1.2 GWh of capacity-market contracted BESS in Poland, demonstrating a replicable European grid storage finance model. ENGIE disclosed it crossed 10 GW of storage capacity worldwide driven by summer 2026 European BESS expansion, while a McKinsey report flagged trade barriers, land constraints and interconnection delays as structural headwinds raising US solar LCOE 15–20% from 2023 levels despite continued technology cost reductions.

items.source: Adani Green Energy / ESS News / PV Magazine India
items.headline: Adani Green Energy Khavda BESS Expands to 6.63 GWh — World’s Largest Single-Location Battery Outside China; Over 50% of India’s Operational BESS at One Site; 14 Months From First Construction Start
items.summary: Adani Green Energy Ltd (AGEL) expanded its operational BESS capacity at Khavda, Gujarat from 3.55 GWh to 6.63 GWh on October 2, 2026, commissioning the new BESS block in just 10 months from the start of its construction. Khavda now holds the world's largest operational single-location battery installation outside China. AGEL accounts for more than 50% of India's total operational BESS capacity of approximately 12.6 GWh. The milestone was reached 14 months after on-site BESS construction first began at the Khavda complex. AGEL previously set the world's single-location BESS record in May 2026 at 3.37 GWh; the October 2 commissioning nearly doubled the installed capacity. Khavda hosts one of the world's largest co-located renewable energy complexes, with solar, wind and now over 6.6 GWh of dispatchable battery storage enabling grid-balancing and evening peak service for Gujarat and national grid operators.

items.headline: Northland Power Closes CAD$185 Million Financing for 300 MW/1.2 GWh Poland BESS (Kamionka + Mieczysláwów); 17-Year Capacity Market Contracts; Green Loan Structure; Government Grants from Polish National Environmental Fund
items.summary: Northland Power closed approximately CAD$185 million (approximately PLN 500 million) in project financing on September 30, 2026 for two BESS projects in Poland: Kamionka (100 MW / 400 MWh) and Mieczysławów (200 MW / 800 MWh). Both projects carry 17-year capacity market contracts with the Polish electricity system operator and are structured as green loans from undisclosed Canadian and Polish financial institutions, supplemented by government grants from Poland's National Fund for Environmental Protection and Water Management. Both projects are under construction with commercial operation targeted for 2028. The capacity market contracting structure provides long-term revenue certainty that underpins project finance — a model being replicated across Central and Eastern European BESS deployment where wholesale price volatility limits merchant-only financing.

items.headline: ENGIE Exceeds 10 GW of Storage Capacity Worldwide; Summer 2026 European BESS Expansion Drives Milestone; Spain and France Portfolios Cross 1 GW; Group Storage Spans Pumped Hydro, Batteries and Demand Response
items.summary: ENGIE announced it has exceeded 10 GW of total storage capacity worldwide, driven by summer 2026 BESS expansion across Europe. The portfolio spans pumped hydropower, utility-scale batteries and demand-response aggregation. In Spain, ENGIE acquired 388 MW / 1.2 GWh of BESS projects in Andalusia in April 2026 and entered a 625 MWh tolling agreement with developer Ignis in July 2026, together pushing its European BESS portfolio past 1 GW. The 10 GW global milestone encompasses operating and contracted capacity across multiple continents and storage technologies. ENGIE's storage expansion reflects the accelerating European market for grid-balancing services as renewable penetration pushes intraday price volatility higher and capacity market reforms across Spain, France and the UK reward dispatchable storage.

items.headline: U.S. Solar and Storage Face Cost Headwinds Under Fragmented Trade Policy: McKinsey Report; Tariff-Driven Equipment Inflation, Land Constraints and 4.5-Year Average Interconnection Queue Raises LCOE 15–20% from 2023; 120 GW Pipeline Stalled
items.summary: A McKinsey & Company report published October 2, 2026 finds that despite record-pace solar and battery storage additions in the United States, three structural constraints add significant friction: trade-policy fragmentation driving equipment cost inflation as domestic content provisions and tariffs diverge across IRA implementation; limited land availability in high-resource, low-congestion grid zones near load centers; and grid interconnection delays now averaging 4.5 years for utility-scale projects nationally. U.S. solar LCOE is now 15–20% higher in nominal terms than 2023 levels due to these factors, partially eroding gains from continued technology improvement. The authors project that addressing grid queue reform and tariff certainty would unlock an estimated 120 GW of stalled project pipeline by 2029. The report recommends accelerated FERC Order 1920 implementation and updated domestic content waivers as the highest-priority policy levers.

items.headline: Renalfa IPP and Eurowind Inaugurate 242 MWp Solar + 773 MWh BESS Hybrid Park in Bulgaria; Among Europe’s Largest Operational Hybrid Renewable Parks; Day-Ahead and Balancing Market Revenue Stack
items.summary: Romanian independent power producer Renalfa IPP and Danish developer Eurowind Energy inaugurated a large-scale hybrid renewable energy park in Bulgaria in October 2026, combining 242 MWp of solar PV with 773 MWh of battery energy storage — among the largest co-located solar-plus-storage facilities in operational service in Europe. The project is structured to optimize revenues across day-ahead energy markets and balancing services, with the BESS enabling intraday dispatch flexibility. Bulgaria has emerged as a significant European BESS market following grid interconnection upgrades and integration into the European balancing platform. The project joins a growing cohort of 200+ MWh co-located storage parks in Central and Eastern Europe, signaling the regional maturation of hybrid renewable development beyond the UK, Germany and Iberia.

science.overview_html: Two new Nature Climate Change studies converge on accelerating heat exposure: Luo et al. find the global heatwave season has lengthened by 39 days over 45 years — onset advancing roughly two weeks, the last heatwave ending nearly four weeks later — while a companion study documents up to 50 additional heat stress days per year in some regions, with the hottest nights warming faster (0.32°C/decade) than the hottest days (0.27°C/decade). On the AI-weather front, ECMWF’s AIFS-DOP demonstrates that an ML model trained solely on observations — bypassing NWP reanalysis entirely — can match medium-range IFS forecast skill, a conceptual breakthrough with implications for data-sparse regions. A new Nature Communications study bridges the weather–climate forecasting divide by demonstrating AI skill out to 90 days, challenging the traditional operational boundary between NWP and seasonal prediction.

items.headline: Earlier and Faster Heatwave Onset on Land (Nature Climate Change, 2026): Season Lengthened 39 Days in 45 Years; Onset 3.29 Days Earlier Per Decade; 92% of Global Land Shows Longer Season; Onset Speed Also Accelerating, Shrinking Response Window
items.meta: Luo et al. · Nature Climate Change (2026) · doi:10.1038/s41558-026-02762-2
items.summary: A Nature Climate Change study analyzed global climate data from 1979 to 2023, examining changes in heatwave season onset and end dates and the onset speed of the first heatwave each year. Findings: the first heatwave of each season arrived 3.29 days earlier per decade while the last ended 5.41 days later per decade — a combined lengthening of 8.71 days per decade; over the full 45-year period, the first heatwave advanced roughly two weeks, the last ended nearly four weeks later, and the season lengthened by about 39 days. These trends covered 72% of global land (earlier onset), 79.6% (later ending) and 92.1% (longer season), with greatest changes in dryland regions. A newly identified trend toward faster heatwave onset speed is a critical finding for emergency preparedness: the time available for heat emergency mobilization is shrinking even as heatwave frequency increases. The study received wide public media coverage for its direct implications for public health planning and heat action frameworks.

items.headline: Global Heat Stress Intensification and Expanding Human Footprint (Nature Climate Change, Vol. 16): Up to 50 Additional Heat Stress Days Per Year in Some Regions; Hottest Nights Warming Faster Than Days (0.32 vs. 0.27°C/Decade); Compound Daytime–Nighttime Events Rising Sharply
items.meta: Multiple authors · Nature Climate Change Vol. 16, pp. 989–996 (2026) · doi:10.1038/s41558-026-02670-5
items.summary: A Nature Climate Change study examining global heat stress from 1950 to the present analyzed daytime extremes, nocturnal heat and compound daytime–nighttime heat events. Key findings: heat stress days increased by up to 50 per year in the most-impacted regions (parts of South Asia, sub-Saharan Africa and the Arabian Peninsula); tropical nights are warming faster than the hottest days, at 0.32°C per decade versus 0.27°C per decade — a pattern with serious implications for human thermal recovery during heatwaves; and compound daytime–nighttime events (which prevent nocturnal cooling recovery) increased sharply in frequency since the 2000s. The study documents pronounced spatial inequality: low- and middle-income countries face disproportionate exposure even as total global heat stress expands. ECMWF published a public summary linking the paper's findings to operational forecasting of heat-health risk and extreme event guidance.

items.headline: AIFS-DOP (arXiv 2606.19093): ECMWF ML Model Trained Only on Observations Matches IFS Medium-Range Skill; Bypasses ERA5 Reanalysis; 40-Year Harmonized Observation Dataset; Competitive at Day 5–10 Upper-Air and Surface — Conceptual Breakthrough for Data-Sparse Regions
items.summary: The AIFS-DOP paper documents ECMWF's development of an ML weather model trained directly on a 40-year harmonized dataset of gridded Earth system observations — without any NWP reanalysis or model output as training targets. All leading MLWP models (GraphCast, Pangu-Weather, FourCastNet, AIFS) are trained on ERA5 reanalysis, which is itself a product of the IFS data assimilation system; AIFS-DOP is the first competitive model to break this dependency. The demonstration shows the observation-trained model matches or surpasses ECMWF IFS medium-range forecast skill for key upper-air and surface headline scores when scored over 2021–2022. The conceptual implications are significant: for monitoring-sparse regions of the ocean and developing nations where the observation–reanalysis–model chain is weakest, an observation-only trained model offers a path to competitive forecasting without dependence on resource-intensive global NWP reanalysis infrastructure. ECMWF's AIFS-DOP update was covered in ECMWF Newsletter No. 182 and 186.

items.headline: Bridging the Weather and Climate Divide with Artificial Intelligence (Nature Communications, 2026): Transformer Framework Shows Significant Skill 7–90 Days; ENSO State and MJO Phase Conditioning; Challenges the Traditional NWP–Seasonal Prediction Boundary
items.summary: A Nature Communications study presents an AI framework bridging the gap between medium-range weather forecasting (days 1–15) and seasonal climate prediction (months 1–6), demonstrating skill across the traditionally underserved 'seamless' timescales of 7–90 days. The transformer-based architecture is trained on ERA5 reanalysis, initialized from operational analyses, and conditioned on large-scale climate drivers including ENSO state and Madden-Julian Oscillation phase. Against competitive benchmarks, the model shows significant skill in predicting weekly-mean temperature and precipitation anomalies out to 90 days, particularly in ENSO-influenced tropical and subtropical regions. The authors argue that the traditional weather–climate operational boundary is an artifact of separate modeling infrastructure rather than a fundamental physical limit, and that ML may be the tool to finally bridge it operationally. The result has direct relevance for subseasonal-to-seasonal (S2S) forecast products used in agriculture, energy trading and disaster preparedness.

items.headline: Bridging Short- and Medium-Range Weather Forecasting with Machine Learning (arXiv 2608.26822): Unified Architecture Across 0–15 Day Range; Reduces Spin-Up Artefacts at Forecast Handoff; Outperforms Separate Short/Medium Models at Transition Lead Times (Days 2–5)
items.summary: An arXiv preprint presents a unified ML architecture for seamless weather forecasting across the 0–15 day range, addressing the 'handoff problem' between short-range models (optimized for day 0–3 high-resolution detail) and medium-range global models (optimized for day 5–15 synoptic accuracy). The hierarchical transformer architecture with scale-specific heads is jointly trained on both short and medium-range verification targets. Results show that the unified model reduces the spin-up artefacts that appear when forecast systems transition between short and medium-range models, and outperforms separate specialized models at transition lead times (days 2–5) on RMSE metrics for 500 hPa geopotential, 850 hPa temperature and 10 m wind speed. The approach contributes to growing operational interest in 'seamless' ML prediction systems that eliminate complex handoff logic between the short and medium NWP model chains maintained by most operational centers.

items.title: Maximum Information Launches PsiClone: Live Tropical Cyclone Portfolio Exposure Platform; 15-Day Ensemble Analytics for Insurers and Reinsurers; MVP Ahead of 2026 Hurricane Season; Humanitarian Pilots for Anticipatory Finance
items.body_html: Maximum Information launched PsiClone, a live event monitoring platform that continuously analyses evolving storm forecasts against insurance portfolios in real time. Built for use before and during active catastrophe events, PsiClone extends monitoring visibility up to 15 days ahead using continuous ensemble forecast analytics, enabling underwriters, claims teams and catastrophe managers to identify exposure hotspots and mobilise response operations earlier. The platform is particularly timely during the current Western Pacific typhoon season: with Typhoon Choi-Wan threatening Ogasawara and the JTWC tracking two active systems this week, real-time ensemble-based exposure monitoring provides portfolio risk managers with the ability to triage accounts before storm landfall. PsiClone was launched as an MVP ahead of the 2026 North Atlantic hurricane season, with additional capabilities under active development. Humanitarian pilots for disaster risk management and anticipatory financing ahead of the Southern Hemisphere cyclone season are also under way.

items.title: KatRisk Joins Verisk Model Exchange: Third-Party Multi-Peril Cat Models (Flood, Surge, TC Wind, SCS, Wildfire, Earthquake; ~100 Countries) Now Available Alongside Verisk’s Own Models in Vendor-Neutral Open-Standards Platform
items.body_html: KatRisk announced its agreement to join Verisk Model Exchange on May 26, 2026, expanding the platform with independent multi-peril catastrophe models covering inland flood, storm surge, tropical cyclone wind, severe convective storm, wildfire and earthquake across approximately 100 countries. Verisk Model Exchange uses open standards so that third-party models run on a consistent financial engine, enabling insurers and reinsurers to evaluate multiple independent views of risk within a single governed environment — reducing the need to maintain separate vendor integrations for each model. The addition is particularly notable for secondary perils and international markets where independent model views have historically been limited. This comes as Verisk raised its global modeled average annual insured loss to $171 billion and Moody’s RMS prepares to unveil a completely rebuilt high-definition North Atlantic Hurricane model with unified wind-and-flood solution at Exceedance 2026.

items.title: Verisk Raises Global Modeled Catastrophe Losses to $171 Billion Average Annual Insured Loss — Up $19 Billion Year-on-Year; Severe Convective Storms Now Most Expensive Hazard of 21st Century, Surpassing Tropical Cyclones
items.body_html: Verisk published its 2026 Global Modeled Catastrophe Losses report on September 1, raising the modeled expected average annual insured loss to $171 billion — up $19 billion from the prior year’s estimate. The report confirms that severe convective storms have overtaken tropical cyclones as the most expensive insured hazard of the 21st century by average annual loss. The revised estimate incorporates updated secondary-peril growth trends, post-event loss amplification assumptions, and climate trend adjustments for perils where attribution studies provide actuarially defensible adjustments to hazard frequency and severity. Separately, Moody’s previewed a completely rebuilt high-definition North Atlantic Hurricane model at its Exceedance 2026 conference, integrating inland flood with wind in a unified solution for the first time, with certification expected before the 2027 hurricane season.

items.title: Climate Tech VC Funding Hits $26.1 Billion in H1 2026, Up 55% Year-on-Year Per CTVC; Earth Observation Funding Triples; AI Data Centers Drive Grid and Storage Investment; Weather and Climate Data Startups Compete for Capital Including WindBorne, Atmo and Brightband
items.body_html: CTVC’s H1 2026 climate tech funding report documents $26.1 billion invested in the first half of 2026 — up 55% year-on-year — with AI data center power demand as the single largest driver through grid infrastructure, long-duration storage and nuclear revival investment. Earth observation and geospatial data companies attracted three times their H1 2025 funding level as institutional investors moved to add real-time climate and weather data assets to their portfolios. Within the weather sector, the CTVC analysis notes several 2026 series raises including WindBorne’s $37 million raise for its atmospheric balloon network, alongside Atmo AI and Brightband, signalling a wave of AI-native weather startups competing for the commercial weather intelligence and renewable energy forecasting market alongside established providers like The Weather Company and tomorrow.io.
